records.header: M E 323 Engineering Thermodynamics (5)
records.text: M E 323 Engineering Thermodynamics (5) Engineering thermodynamics, including thermodynamic concepts and properties, the first and second laws of thermodynamics, energy conversion, refrigeration, humidification, and combustion. Engineering design applications. Course overlaps with: B ME 331 and TME 331. Prerequisite: either CHEM 142, CHEM 143, or CHEM 145; either MATH 126 or MATH 136; and either PHYS 121 or PHYS 141.

records.text: M E 331 Introduction to Heat Transfer (4) Study of heat transfer by conduction, radiation, and convection; elementary heat-exchanger design. Course overlaps with: B ME 333 and TME 433. Prerequisite: either M E 333 or CEE 342.

records.header: M E 333 Introduction to Fluid Mechanics (5)
records.text: M E 333 Introduction to Fluid Mechanics (5) Introduction to the basic fluid laws and their application. Conservation equations, dynamic similarity, potential flow, boundary-layer concepts, effects of friction, compressible flow, fluid machinery, measurement techniques. Course overlaps with: B ME 332; TCE 347; and TME 332. Prerequisite: AMATH 301; M E 323; and either MATH 207 or AMATH 351.

records.text: M E 341 Energy and Environment (3) NSc Energy use. Fossil energy conversion. Oil, gas, coal resources. Air impacts. Nuclear energy principles, reactors, fuel cycle. Prerequisite: either MATH 112, MATH 124, MATH 134, or Q SCI 291; either CHEM 120, CHEM 142, CHEM 143, CHEM 145, PHYS 114, PHYS 121, or PHYS 141. Offered: jointly with CHEM E 341/ENVIR 341; A.

records.title: Mechanics of Materials Laboratory
records.header: M E 354 Mechanics of Materials Laboratory (5)
records.text: M E 354 Mechanics of Materials Laboratory (5) Properties and behavior of engineering materials including stress-strain relations, strength, deformation mechanisms, strength, deformation, fracture, creep, and cyclic fatigue. Introduces experimental techniques common to structural engineering, interpretation of experimental data, comparison of measurements to numerical/analytical predictions, and formal, engineering report writing. Lecture and laboratory. Prerequisite: MSE 170, CEE 220.

records.header: M E 355 Introduction to Manufacturing Processes (4)
records.text: M E 355 Introduction to Manufacturing Processes (4) Study of manufacturing processes, including interrelationships between the properties of the material, the manufacturing process, and the design of components. Interpretation of experimental data, comparison of measurements to numerical/analytical predictions, and formal, engineering report writing. Course overlaps with: TME 345 and TME 445. Prerequisite: M E 354.

records.header: M E 356 Machine Design Analysis (4)
records.text: M E 356 Machine Design Analysis (4) Analysis, design, and selection of mechanical and electromechanical subsystems and elements, such as gears, linkages, cams, motors, and bearings. Course overlaps with: TME 341 and TME 342. Prerequisite: M E 354.

records.header: M E 373 Introduction to System Dynamics (5)
records.text: M E 373 Introduction to System Dynamics (5) Mathematical modeling, analysis, and design of physical dynamic systems involving energy storage and transfer by lumped-parameter linear elements. Time-domain response by analytical methods and numeric simulation. Laboratory experiments. Prerequisite: either AMATH 351 or MATH 207; either AMATH 352 or MATH 208; E E 215; and M E 230.
records.prerequisiteText: either AMATH 351 or MATH 207; either AMATH 352 or MATH 208; E E 215; and M E 230.

records.header: M E 374 Systems Dynamic Analysis and Design (5)
records.text: M E 374 Systems Dynamic Analysis and Design (5) Extension of M E 373. Frequency response analysis, generalized impedance concepts and applications, Fourier series analysis and Laplace transform techniques. Modeling and analysis of electromechanical actuators and rotating machinery. Laboratory experiments and design projects. Prerequisite: AMATH 301; M E 373.

records.title: Engineering Experiential Learning
records.header: M E 398 Engineering Experiential Learning (1, max. 20)
records.text: M E 398 Engineering Experiential Learning (1, max. 20) Team-based projects where students apply principles of engineering, design, manufacturing, and entrepreneurship to solve real-world challenges and gain hands-on experience. Projects are overseen by faculty and may involve mentoring from external organizations. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AWSpS.

records.title: Additive Manufacturing: Materials, Processing and Applications
records.header: M E 402 Additive Manufacturing: Materials, Processing and Applications (3)
records.text: M E 402 Additive Manufacturing: Materials, Processing and Applications (3) Additive manufacturing processes for polymers, metals, ceramics and composite materials. Operating principles, key process parameters important to the part build process, and the importance of design. Microstructure of the build parts, dependence on processing conditions, the mechanical and physical properties, defects and relevant post-processing treatments for each material system. Hybrid processes, and adoption in various fields. Offered: jointly with MSE 489; Sp.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Polymer Physics
records.header: M E 409 Polymer Physics (3)
records.text: M E 409 Polymer Physics (3) Dives into the statistical-mechanical, thermodynamic, and continuum theories that describe the structure, dynamics, and rheology of polymeric materials. Focuses on developing a deep conceptual understanding of the theoretical frameworks and simulation methods used in polymer research and connecting these to experimental methods. Teaches techniques to analyze and predict the behavior of specific polymer systems. Prerequisite: M E 323. Offered: jointly with CHEM 435.

records.title: Nanodevices: Design and Manufacture
records.header: M E 410 Nanodevices: Design and Manufacture (3)
records.text: M E 410 Nanodevices: Design and Manufacture (3) Examines design, fabrication, and manufacture of nano devices with state-of-the-art nanotechnology. Covers classification and selection of nanoscale materials and manufacturing methods: Includes nanodevice design projects. Offered: A.

records.title: Biological Frameworks for Engineers
records.header: M E 411 Biological Frameworks for Engineers (3)
records.text: M E 411 Biological Frameworks for Engineers (3) Introduces the fundamentals of biology for an engineer. Covers mechanisms and biomechanics of DNA, proteins, cells, connective tissue, musculoskeletal tissue, and cardiovascular tissue, integration principles of living systems, structure-function relationships, and techniques to study biology and medicine, and tissue engineering. Offered: A.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Biomechanics of Movement
records.header: M E 412 Biomechanics of Movement (3)
records.text: M E 412 Biomechanics of Movement (3) Introduction to the dynamics and control of human movement and other biological systems. An overview of the major challenges in movement biomechanics and experience with the engineering tools we use to address these challenges. Course includes weekly assignment, hands-on labs, and a final project. Course overlaps with: TME 450. Prerequisite: M E 374. Offered: W.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Engineering Innovation in Health
records.header: M E 414 Engineering Innovation in Health (3)
records.text: M E 414 Engineering Innovation in Health (3) Introduces the role of innovation and engineering in the design of medical devices and healthcare technologies, applicable both to medical practice and healthcare-focused engineering. May serve as the first course in a medically related senior design project sequence. Discusses medical practice, clinical needs finding, FDA regulation, insurance reimbursement, intellectual property, and the medical device design process. Recommended: M E 123 and M E 354. Offered: A.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Introduction to Cell Mechanics
records.header: M E 415 Introduction to Cell Mechanics (3)
records.text: M E 415 Introduction to Cell Mechanics (3) Emphasizes mechanical engineering principles in the cell as a dynamic system. Covers general forces in cell processes, techniques, and models to assess cell mechanics; techniques and models to assess single cell forces; biomaterials/microenvironments to assess cell mechanics; and introduction to mechanosensitive receptors and corresponding signaling pathways. Recommended: M E 411. Offered: Sp.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Mechanobiology
records.header: M E 416 Mechanobiology (3)
records.text: M E 416 Mechanobiology (3) Applications of mechanobiology principles to the development and pathophysiology of tissues and body systems, including orthopaedic and cardiovascular tissues, wound healing and fibrosis, cancer, and regenerative biology and engineering. Recommended: either M E 411, M E 415, or BIOEN 315 (or equivalent); BIOEN 325 (or equivalent); and BIOEN 326 (or equivalent). Offered: jointly with BIOEN 426.
records.recommendedPreparationText: either M E 411, M E 415, or BIOEN 315 (or equivalent); BIOEN 325 (or equivalent); and BIOEN 326 (or equivalent).

records.title: Materials Science and Engineering for Batteries
records.header: M E 417 Materials Science and Engineering for Batteries (3)
records.text: M E 417 Materials Science and Engineering for Batteries (3) Fundamentals of battery materials, battery chemistry, and applications. Topics include history and development of lithium-ion batteries and industry; materials science for electrodes and electrolytes; sciences for processing and manufacturing of battery materials, advanced battery chemistries, and cell design and fabrication. Covers the requirements in areas such as electric vehicles, medical devices, grid storage, aviation, and robotics. Offered: jointly with MSE 417.

records.text: M E 425 HVAC Engineering (4) Heating, ventilating, and air conditioning of built environment. Human comfort, psychometric processes, load computations, fluid distribution, and controls. Design analysis of HVAC system is taught in the lectures and applied in the class project. Course overlaps with: B ME 435 and TME 435. Prerequisite: M E 323; M E 331.

records.text: M E 426 Renewable Energy II (3) Explores renewable energy principles and practices of energy conversion, focusing on energy conversion from wind and water. Prerequisite: M E 333.

records.text: M E 430 Advanced Energy Conversion Systems (4) Covers advanced energy conversion systems and technologies, including high efficiency combined cycles, advanced rankine, integrated gasification combined cycle, nuclear, biomass thermal conversion, and fuels cells. records.text: M E 431 Advanced Fluid Mechanics (4) Advanced topics in fluid mechanics, including kinematics, potential theory and vortex dynamics, viscous flow, turbulence, experimental and numerical methods, and design. Prerequisite: M E 333.

records.title: Advanced Mechanics of Materials and Solids
records.header: M E 440 Advanced Mechanics of Materials and Solids (3)
records.text: M E 440 Advanced Mechanics of Materials and Solids (3) Study of mechanics of deformable bodies, including three-dimensional stress and strain tensors and their transformations. Equations of compatibility, continuity and equilibrium. Elastic constants. Failure criteria including fracture, yield, and instability. Deflection relations for complex loading and shapes. Indeterminate problems. Design applications and numerical methods. Course overlaps with: B ME 341 and TME 341. Prerequisite: M E 354.

records.title: Introduction to Biomechanics
records.header: M E 445 Introduction to Biomechanics (4)
records.text: M E 445 Introduction to Biomechanics (4) Presents the mechanical behavior of tissues in the body and the application to design of prostheses. Tissues studies include bone, skin, fascia, ligaments, tendons, heart valves, and blood vessels. Discussion of the structure of these tissues and their mechanical response to different loading configurations. An important part of the class is a final project. Offered: jointly with BIOEN 440; Sp.

records.header: M E 450 Introduction to Composite Materials and Design (3)
records.text: M E 450 Introduction to Composite Materials and Design (3) Explores stress and strain analysis of continuous fiber composite materials. Covers orthotropic elasticity, lamination theory, failure criterion, and design philosophies, as applied to structural polymeric composites.

records.text: M E 459 Introduction to Fracture Mechanics (3) Deformation processes leading to fracture, and linear elastic fracture mechanics. Fatigue crack propagation. Fracture control and failure analysis. Prerequisite: M E 354; M E 356.

records.text: M E 461 Mechanics of Thin Films (3) Provides an overview of the thin film deposition processes; the stress and microstructure development during film growth; the mechanisms of adhesion; delamination and fracture; and the state-of-the-art characterization techniques for the microstructure and mechanical properties of thin films, coatings, and nanomaterials. Dynamics of instrument response; generalized performance analysis of sensor systems; theory of transducers for motion, force, pressure, flow, and other measurements. Lecture and laboratory. records.header: M E 477 Embedded Computing in Mechanical Systems (4)
records.text: M E 477 Embedded Computing in Mechanical Systems (4) Analysis of electromechanical systems employing microcomputers for control or data acquisition. Microcomputer architecture, memory organization, C language programming, interfaces, and communications. Particular emphasis on design of hardware and software interfaces for real-time interaction with mechanical systems. Weekly laboratory. Course overlaps with: B ME 460 and TME 441. Prerequisite: M E 374.

Applications in all areas of mechanical engineering, including mechanics of solids, heat transfer, and design of dynamical systems. Weekly computer exercises. Course equivalent to: TME 478. Prerequisite: M E 123; M E 374; and either MATH 208 or AMATH 352.

Computer-aided design, engineering, drafting, and manufacturing; computer-aided design systems, geometry, computer graphics, hardware, computer-aided vehicle/system design synthesis. Topics include engineering design process and methodology, overview of several frameworks and tools common in mechanical engineering, teamwork and project management, and technical communication.
